issuer: the Registrar of Motor Vehicles of Norfolk Island
note: Read 2026-10-30 in the Federal Register of Legislation (legislation.gov.au, through its API; the Norfolk Island Regional Council's site answered 403): the Traffic Act 2010 (NI), a law continued in force by the Norfolk Island Continued Laws Ordinance 2015, compilation 7 of 10 July 2021 (title C2015Q00249, register id C2021Q00022, listed in force; prepared by the Office of Parliamentary Counsel). The Registrar of Motor Vehicles, appointed under s 5, issues every licence. A learners licence from 15 (s 16(3)); a provisional licence to someone over the age of 16 who has held a learners licence for at least 3 months (s 16A(1)(c)), in force 2 years (s 16A(4)); a drivers licence only to someone who has held a provisional licence for the 2 years before applying (s 17(3A)), unless they held a drivers licence before (s 17(3B)). The full licence's age is built from those stages, 16 and 2 years, 18 (a reading: 'over the age of 16' held as 16, as Pitcairn's 'over the age of 15' was held as 15). A drivers licence lasts 3 years, or 2 if its holder is 70 or more at its issue (s 17(4); the shorter term not held). Every licence is issued on payment of 'the approved fee'; the Traffic (Fees) Regulations (NI) are listed as repealed and the fee now charged wasn't found: fee null. The Australian dollar is the island's currency.

sources.said: Compilation No. 7 ... Compilation date: 10 July 2021 ... The Chief Executive Officer shall, by notice in the Gazette, appoint a person to be the Registrar of Motor Vehicles. ... The Registrar shall not issue a learners licence to an applicant unless satisfied that the applicant has attained the age of 15 years. ... (i) is over the age of 16 years; ... (ii) has held a learners licence for at least 3 months; ... a provisional licence remains in force for a period of 2 years after its date of issue. ... the Registrar shall not issue a drivers licence unless the Registrar is satisfied that the applicant has held a provisional licence for a period of 2 years immediately before the making of the application. ... a drivers licence remains in force for a period of — ... (a) 3 years; or ... on payment of the approved fee,
